{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go",
      "line": 87,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Failed device tagging is cached, allowing anonymous device limit bypass",
      "body": "In tagDeviceUI, the local cache entry for a device ID is written before the database upsert. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the entry is not removed. Anonymous.Authenticate fails the first request, but a retry with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id header gets a cache hit, TagDevice returns nil, and the request is authenticated even though the device was not stored and the configured limit should block it. The same caching of failed operations also hides transient database errors for the cache TTL."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go",
      "line": 119,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Client-controlled device ID can exhaust the anonymous device limit",
      "body": "The anonymous device identifier is supplied by the client in the X-Grafana-Device-Id header. With device_limit enabled, unauthenticated callers can create arbitrary unique device IDs until the configured number of active devices is reached. Those attacker-created records remain active for the 30-day window, after which new legitimate devices receive ErrDeviceLimitReached and cannot authenticate, causing a denial of service for new anonymous users."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go",
      "line": 110,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Device-limit check and insert are not atomic",
      "body": "CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices and then, if the count is below the limit, executes the upsert as a separate operation. There is no transaction, row lock, or conditional insert, so concurrent new devices can all pass the count check and insert. The active device count can therefore exceed device_limit under normal concurrent traffic."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go",
      "line": 44,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Device limit adds synchronous database work to anonymous authentication",
      "body": "The PR changes anonymous device tagging from an asynchronous goroutine to a synchronous step in Authenticate. When device_limit is enabled, each uncached device performs a COUNT over anon_device and an upsert before the request can proceed. For high-traffic anonymous instances, especially if updated_at is not efficiently indexed, this can add significant latency and database load to anonymous authentication."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts",
      "line": 200,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Frontend type for anonymousDeviceLimit does not match backend JSON",
      "body": "GrafanaConfig declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined, but the Go FrontendSettingsDTO uses a non-pointer int64 without omitempty, so the backend always sends a number, with 0 meaning unlimited. Frontend code that checks for undefined to determine whether a limit is configured will not work; the contract should either use a pointer/omitempty or document 0 as unlimited."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/setting/setting.go",
      "line": 1654,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Negative device_limit silently disables the limit",
      "body": "device_limit is read with MustInt64(0) and enforcement only occurs when the value is greater than zero. A negative configuration value is accepted and silently treated as unlimited, which can hide operator mistakes. The setting should be validated as non-negative."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl_test.go",
      "line": 120,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests cover device-limit failures in AnonDeviceService",
      "body": "The tests cover successful tagging and a store-level limit, but do not exercise AnonDeviceService.tagDeviceUI when CreateOrUpdateDevice fails. In particular there is no test that a failed device-limit attempt is not cached, which is the behavior that allows the limit bypass in impl.go."
    }

findings.title: Failed device tagging is cached, allowing anonymous device limit bypass
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI, the local cache entry for a device ID is written before the database upsert. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the entry is not removed. Anonymous.Authenticate fails the first request, but a retry with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id header gets a cache hit, TagDevice returns nil, and the request is authenticated even though the device was not stored and the configured limit should block it. The same caching of failed operations also hides transient database errors for the cache TTL.

findings.title: Client-controlled device ID can exhaust the anonymous device limit
findings.body: The anonymous device identifier is supplied by the client in the X-Grafana-Device-Id header. With device_limit enabled, unauthenticated callers can create arbitrary unique device IDs until the configured number of active devices is reached. Those attacker-created records remain active for the 30-day window, after which new legitimate devices receive ErrDeviceLimitReached and cannot authenticate, causing a denial of service for new anonymous users.

findings.title: Device-limit check and insert are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices and then, if the count is below the limit, executes the upsert as a separate operation. There is no transaction, row lock, or conditional insert, so concurrent new devices can all pass the count check and insert. The active device count can therefore exceed device_limit under normal concurrent traffic.

findings.title: Device limit adds synchronous database work to anonymous authentication
findings.body: The PR changes anonymous device tagging from an asynchronous goroutine to a synchronous step in Authenticate. When device_limit is enabled, each uncached device performs a COUNT over anon_device and an upsert before the request can proceed. For high-traffic anonymous instances, especially if updated_at is not efficiently indexed, this can add significant latency and database load to anonymous authentication.

findings.title: Frontend type for anonymousDeviceLimit does not match backend JSON
findings.body: GrafanaConfig declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined, but the Go FrontendSettingsDTO uses a non-pointer int64 without omitempty, so the backend always sends a number, with 0 meaning unlimited. Frontend code that checks for undefined to determine whether a limit is configured will not work; the contract should either use a pointer/omitempty or document 0 as unlimited.

findings.title: Negative device_limit silently disables the limit
findings.body: device_limit is read with MustInt64(0) and enforcement only occurs when the value is greater than zero. A negative configuration value is accepted and silently treated as unlimited, which can hide operator mistakes. The setting should be validated as non-negative.

findings.title: No tests cover device-limit failures in AnonDeviceService
findings.body: The tests cover successful tagging and a store-level limit, but do not exercise AnonDeviceService.tagDeviceUI when CreateOrUpdateDevice fails. In particular there is no test that a failed device-limit attempt is not cached, which is the behavior that allows the limit bypass in impl.go.
